Use plasma-enhanced magnetron sputtering for uniform deposition, targeting a surface coverage of ≥90% as confirmed by XPS analysis. The intervention leverages zwitterionic hydration layers to suppress biofouling via steric and electrostatic repulsion while inhibiting mineral scaling through charge regulation.

**PARAMETERS:**
- Polymer type: poly(carboxybetaine methacrylate) — EVIDENCE-BACKED [doi:10.1016/j.cis.2026.104052]
- Grafting density: 0.3–0.5 chains/nm² — ASSUMPTION
- Brush thickness: 10–15 nm — (ASSUMPTION — value not stated in the cited record)- Surface coverage: ≥90% — (ASSUMPTION — value not stated in the cited record)- Deposition method: plasma-enhanced magnetron sputtering — (ASSUMPTION — value not stated in the cited record)**EXPECTED EFFECT:**
Maintain normalized differential pressure within 5% over 6 weeks (vs. 20% increase observed in baseline) while preserving ≥45% permeate recovery. Biofouling and scale accumulation will be reduced by ≥80% due to hydration-layer stabilization and charge-neutrality, as supported by zwitterionic fouling suppression mechanisms in [doi:10.1016/j.cis.2026.104052].

**CONSTRAINT RESPECT:**
- Permeate recovery ≥45%: Zwitterionic brushes preserve hydraulic permeability via steric repulsion without pore blockage (ASSUMPTION — value not stated in the cited record).
- CIP ≤ every 3 months: Fouling suppression reduces cleaning frequency by ≥75% (ASSUMPTION based on 80% fouling reduction and 6-week test window).
- RO desalination train: Intervention targets lead membranes only, maintaining system architecture.

**FALSIFICATION TEST:**
Test protocol: Operate modified RO train at 25°C feed temperature (standard desalination conditions) for 6 weeks with brackish water feed (35,000 ppm TDS). Sample size n=3 identical membrane modules. Pass/fail criterion: Normalized differential pressure increase ≤5% (baseline + 3σ from 14 days of healthy data) and permeate recovery ≥45%.
